knowledge:
- key_parameters: dataT=Matrix or data frame of cytosolic mRNA levels ;; dataP=Matrix or data frame of translationally active mRNA levels (polysome or ribosome-bound mRNA) ;; phenoVec=Vector specifying the sample class/phenotype for each sample ;; useRVM=Logical indicating whether to use the Random Variance Model to adjust within-gene variance ;; nDfbSimData=Number of simulated data sets to generate for dfbeta outlier frequency estimation
- alternatives: Direct comparison of translationally active mRNA (ignores cytosolic changes, which confounds transcription/stability with translation) ;; Log ratio approach (subtracting log cytosolic from log translationally active mRNA, which can lead to spurious correlations and false conclusions compared to APV)
- when_to_use: When analyzing genome-wide translational control using parallel quantification of cytosolic mRNA and actively translating mRNA (via polysome microarrays or ribosome profiling) with at least 3 replicate experiments per group.
- pitfalls: Outlier samples can generate an excessive number of highly influential data points ;; Systematic errors in polysome fraction cut-offs can cause a high abundance of class-slope interactions ;; Strong deviation of residuals from normality may require alternative normalization ;; Unrealistic slopes (<0 or >1) can affect the analysis and should be filtered or flagged ;; RVM requires the empirical variances to fit a theoretical F-distribution, which is highly sensitive to data normalization.

workflows.name: translational_efficiency_analysis
workflows.intent: Perform quality control, test regression assumptions, and identify significantly translationally regulated genes using APV.
input: dataT (matrix or data frame of cytosolic mRNA levels)
dataP (matrix or data frame of translationally active/polysomal mRNA levels)
phenoVec (character or factor vector of sample phenotypes)
workflows.stages: 1. Perform quality control of influential data points and interactions using anotaPerformQc ;; 2. Assess residual normality using anotaResidOutlierTest ;; 3. Identify significantly translationally regulated genes using anotaGetSigGenes ;; 4. Filter and plot significant genes using anotaPlotSigGenes
workflows.code:
library("anota")
 data(anotaDataSet)
 anotaQcOut <- anotaPerformQc(dataT=anotaDataT[1:200,], dataP=anotaDataP[1:200,], phenoVec=anotaPhenoVec, nDfbSimData=500, useProgBar=FALSE)
 anotaResidOut <- anotaResidOutlierTest(anotaQcObj=anotaQcOut, useProgBar=FALSE)
 anotaSigOut <- anotaGetSigGenes(dataT=anotaDataT[1:200,], dataP=anotaDataP[1:200,], phenoVec=anotaPhenoVec, anotaQcObj=anotaQcOut, useRVM=FALSE, useProgBar=FALSE)
anotaSelected <- anotaPlotSigGenes(anotaSigObj=anotaSigOut, selContr=1, maxP=0.1, minSlope=(-0.5), maxSlope=1.5, selDeltaPT=0.5)
